title: Practice Q09: a label with a serving trap

beats.text: Practice question Q zero nine is worth four marks. Pause the video and try it.

What's asked: the energy in one serving, in kilojoules and in joules. The label gives masses per one hundred grams, and a serving is thirty grams. So we'll find the energy per one hundred grams, then scale.
Predict first. A serving is under a third of one hundred grams, so its energy should be a bit under a third of the per-one-hundred-gram value.

Carbohydrate: forty-eight point zero grams times sixteen is seven hundred and sixty-eight kilojoules. Protein: twelve point zero times seventeen is two hundred and four. Fat: eighteen point zero times thirty-seven is six hundred and sixty-six. Total: one thousand six hundred and thirty-eight kilojoules per one hundred grams.

Now scale to one thirty-gram serving: one thousand six hundred and thirty-eight times thirty point zero over one hundred gives four hundred and ninety-one point four, about four hundred and ninety-one kilojoules. That's just under a third, as predicted.

In joules, multiply by one thousand: four hundred and ninety-one point four kilojoules is four point nine one times ten to the power of five joules. A larger unit to a smaller one, so the number gets bigger.

Marks: two for the weighted sum, one for the serving factor, and one for the conversion to joules. The traps: using the whole ninety-gram packet, which gives about one thousand four hundred and seventy-four kilojoules, or writing four hundred and ninety-one joules when the value is in kilojoules.
